To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) sequencing error rates are 1–4 per kilobase, 2) most errors are contributed to by the ends of single-reads, 3) errors can be predicted with high confidence from quality scores, 4) errors can be masked automatically at low false-positive cost, 5) errors have a significant impact on phylogenomic analyses, and 6) errors can be eliminated at higher cost.

(1) the rate of sequencing errors is low, (2) sequencing error is highly localized, (3) sequencing error is strongly predicted by quality scores (4) sequencing error is predictable based on comparisons across species, (5) automatic methods can mitigate sequencing error, (6) automatic methods for error correction cannot replace the need to increase coverage, and (7) the impact of sequencing errors on phylogenomics can be reduced using our methods.

(1) the rate of sequencing errors in low-coverage assemblies is low enough that the impact of error on downstream analyses can be reduced with automatic methods, and (2) the rate of errors is sufficiently high that it can have substantial impact on downstream analyses if no error mitigation is used.
